request.spec:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now be retired from a date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What it does**
- **Retiring:** each person's row has a date box and a Retire button. If the date is left blank, the sheet's today is used. Retiring writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>` to the audit file.
- **Counts as retired at once:** anyone with a retirement date is retired straight away, even if the date is after the sheet's today. Their row shows retired "yes" and the date; everyone else shows "no" and a blank date.
- **Claims:** a claim dated after the retirement date is refused with the form's error, and nothing is saved or audited. Claims dated on or before it are still allowed, even if added later. The same check applies when a claim is edited and to quick add, which dates claims at the sheet's today.
- **The list:** retired people have no row unless "show retired" is ticked. The box starts off and stays as it is when you load a sheet.
- **Totals:** their claims still count in the overall claimed and due totals and in each period's total.

**Changes by layer**
- **Data:** a new migration, `V16__person_retired.sql`, adds a `retired_from` date to each person.
- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{id}/retire` call. A claim dated after the retirement date is refused with status 422, which the screen turns into its own error message.
- **Screen:** the "show retired" setting is kept in `Session` so loading a sheet doesn't reset it. The list hides retired people only on screen; the totals are still worked out from everyone.

**Choices the request didn't cover:**
- Retiring someone again just moves their date. There is no way to un-retire.
- Claims already dated after the retirement date are kept and keep counting; only new or edited claims are checked.
